title: Field-valued extension over a Kummer sharp pushout
statement:
Let $P,Q,R$ be fs commutative monoids, written additively, with group completion and saturation as in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Let $h:P\to Q$, $k:P\to R$ be homomorphisms, let $\Omega$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $a:Q\to(\Omega,\cdot)$ and $b:R\to(\Omega,\cdot)$ satisfy $ah=bk$. For any such map $e:L\to(\Omega,\cdot)$, define the face $F_e=\{l\in L:e(l)\ne0\}$, the localization $L-F_e=\{l-f:l\in L,f\in F_e\}\subset L^{\rm gp}$, and the sharp monoid $\overline L_e=(L-F_e)/F_e^{\rm gp}$, where the quotient identifies elements differing by an element of $F_e^{\rm gp}$. Suppose the induced map
$$\overline h:\overline P_{ah}\to\overline Q_a$$
is injective and every element of $\overline Q_a$ has a positive multiple in its image. Set $S=Q\amalg_PR$, the quotient of $Q\oplus R$ by the monoid congruence generated by $(h(p),0)\sim(0,k(p))$, and set
$$S^{\rm fs}=\{u\in S^{\rm gp}:\exists n>0,\ nu\in\operatorname{im}(S\to S^{\rm gp})\}.$$
Then there is a monoid homomorphism $d:S^{\rm fs}\to(\Omega,\cdot)$ whose composites with $Q\to S\to S^{\rm fs}$ and $R\to S\to S^{\rm fs}$ are $a$ and $b$, respectively. Neither uniqueness nor any invertibility of the positive multiples in $\Omega$ is asserted.

source.place: VI 2.1, p.71 (Kummer condition on sharp monoids), VIII 3.1.17, p.101 (saturation); algebraic field-extension input for the fs base changes of X 1.8, pp.146--147. Agent formulation and proof in report.md; WANTED a direct published reference for this algebraic lemma.

proof.text: Put $F_P=F_{ah}$, $F_Q=F_a$, $F_R=F_b$. These are faces: a product in a field is nonzero exactly when both factors are nonzero; agreement on $P$ gives $h^{-1}(F_Q)=F_P=k^{-1}(F_R)$. Apply [lem-trf-fs-face-sharpening] to form $A=P-F_P$, $B=Q-F_Q$, $C=R-F_R$, all fs, with unit subgroups $U_A=F_P^{\rm gp}$, $U_B=F_Q^{\rm gp}$, $U_C=F_R^{\rm gp}$. Their sharp quotients are the monoids in the hypothesis, and their group completions are $P^{\rm gp},Q^{\rm gp},R^{\rm gp}$. The maps extend by $f(p-u)=h(p)-h(u)$ and $g(p-u)=k(p)-k(u)$. They are local: if $h(p)-h(u)\in F_Q^{\rm gp}$ then $h(p)\in F_Q$ (the intersection $Q\cap F_Q^{\rm gp}=F_Q$ follows by writing a difference of face elements), so $p\in F_P$; the converse and the $g$ case are the same calculation. Thus $\overline f=\overline h$ is injective and root-cofinal.

source.place: VI 2.1, p.71, with VIII 3.1.1--3.1.2, p.98; localization at nonzero-evaluation faces, agent expansion.

proof.text:
Use the group presentation
$$H=(Q^{\rm gp}\oplus R^{\rm gp})/\{(h^{\rm gp}(p),-k^{\rm gp}(p)):p\in P^{\rm gp}\}.$$
It identifies $H$ with $S^{\rm gp}$: a homomorphism from either group to an abelian group is precisely a pair of homomorphisms from $Q,R$ agreeing on $P$, by the generators and relations of group completion in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Let $i_B,i_C$ be the maps from $B^{\rm gp},C^{\rm gp}$ into $H$, put $M=i_B(B)+i_C(C)$, and $U=i_B(U_B)+i_C(U_C)$. The image of $S$ in $H$ is contained in $M$; no injectivity of $S\to H$ is being assumed.

source.place: VIII 3.1.1--3.1.2, p.98; group presentation of the localized pushout, agent argument.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-local-kummer-pushout-units] to $f:A\to B$ and $g:A\to C$. Its hypotheses were checked in Step 1, and its group presentation is Step 2. Consequently $M\cap(-M)=U$, and $i_B(b)\in U$ is equivalent to $b\in U_B$, while $i_C(c)\in U$ is equivalent to $c\in U_C$. This is the input ensuring that integralization will preserve the prescribed zero locus.

source.place: VI 2.1, p.71, local Kummer algebra for X 1.8, pp.146--147; agent expansion.

proof.text: The formulas $a_B(q-u)=a(q)a(u)^{-1}$ and $b_C(r-v)=b(r)b(v)^{-1}$ are well-defined homomorphisms to $\Omega$: equality of two differences gives equality of the cross-products, and the denominators are nonzero. Their restrictions to $U_B,U_C$ take values in $\Omega^\times$ and agree on $U_A$. They descend to a character $\chi:U\to\Omega^\times$. Indeed, if $(u,v)\in U_B\oplus U_C$ maps to zero in $H$, then $(u,v)=(f^{\rm gp}(p),-g^{\rm gp}(p))$ for some $p\in A^{\rm gp}$. By [lem-trf-fs-face-sharpening], $A^{\rm gp}/U_A=\overline A^{\rm gp}$ and similarly for $B$. The group map $\overline f^{\rm gp}$ is injective: write an element as $x-y$ with $x,y\in\overline A$, and use integrality and injectivity of $\overline f$ if its image vanishes. Since $f^{\rm gp}(p)\in U_B$, it follows that $p\in U_A$. Hence $a_B(u)b_C(v)=a_B(f(p))/b_C(g(p))=1$, proving the required kernel compatibility and descent.

source.place: VIII 3.1.1--3.1.2, p.98; explicit kernel calculation in the group presentation, agent argument.

proof.text:
Set $T=\{x\in H:nx\in M\text{ for some }n>0\}$. It is a submonoid: multiply the two positive witnesses to check closure under sums. Its unit subgroup is
$$T^\times=\{x\in H:nx\in U\text{ for some }n>0\}.$$
Indeed, if $x,-x\in T$, choose a common positive multiple $n$ such that $nx,-nx\in M$; then $nx\in M\cap(-M)=U$ by Step 3. Conversely $nx\in U$ implies $nx,-nx\in M$, so $x,-x\in T$.

source.place: VIII 3.1.17, p.101, saturation; explicit unit-face extension and restriction, agent argument.

proof.text: Define $D:T\to(\Omega,\cdot)$ by $D(x)=\psi(x)$ on $T^\times$ and $D(x)=0$ elsewhere. It preserves the identity since $0\in T^\times$ and $\psi(0)=1$. In a commutative monoid, $x+y$ is a unit exactly when both $x,y$ are units: if $-(x+y)\in T$, then $-x=y-(x+y)\in T$ and $-y=x-(x+y)\in T$; the converse follows by adding inverses. Thus $D(x+y)=D(x)D(y)$ in both cases, so $D$ is a homomorphism.

source.place: VIII 3.1.17, p.101, saturation; explicit unit-face extension and restriction, agent argument.

proof.text: If $i_B(b)\in T^\times$, Step 6 gives $i_B(nb)\in U$ for some $n>0$. Step 3 implies $nb\in U_B$, whence $-b=(n-1)b-nb\in B$ and $b\in U_B$. The converse is immediate, and the identical calculation with $C$ proves its analogue. For $q\in Q\cap U_B=F_Q$, therefore, $D(i_B(q))=\psi(i_B(q))=\chi(i_B(q))=a(q)$. For $q\notin F_Q$, the image is a nonunit in $T$, so both $D(i_B(q))$ and $a(q)$ are zero. Likewise $D(i_C(r))=b(r)$ for every $r\in R$. Finally $S^{\rm fs}\subset T$, since the image of $S$ lies in $M$. The restriction $d=D|_{S^{\rm fs}}$, under $H=S^{\rm gp}$ from Step 2, has the two required composites.
